name: Bog
notes: Ombrotrophic raised/blanket bog: rain-fed acid peat, Sphagnum carpets, cottongrass, heath dwarf shrubs, carnivorous sundews, stunted bog pines. Drawn on Scandinavia/British Isles/Baltic and Canadian muskeg.

growth.juvenile_note: Tiny epigeal seedlings on moss grow only 2.5-15 cm a year. Saplings are narrow, spindly spires with short blue-green needles and a dense, club-like top; lower branches drooping onto the moss often root (layering), ringing an old tree with young clones. Mature trees look like bottle-brushes with a knob of cones at the top.
growth.source: USDA Silvics (Viereck & Johnston): seedlings 2.5 cm/yr on moss, to 15 cm on mineral soil; 12-20 m on good sites; main cone-bearing age 30-250; establishes in 10% of full light; layering common; average max age ~200, up to 280 years

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (pollen late May-early June; cones 1-4 cm, green or purplish when young, seed mature late Aug-early Sep; semi-serotinous cones stay partly closed on the tree for years, holding viable seed up to 25 years and releasing it gradually or after fire; heavy crops every 2-6 years)

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 5-7 cotyledons; in its first year it has single, flat, finely serrated primary needles 2-3 cm long, then short, twisted, blue-green paired needles. Young trees are regular, bushy cones; later the lower branches drop and the crown becomes flat or rounded above a tall trunk whose upper bark is orange and flaky.
growth.source: Wikipedia (to 35 m, over 45 m on the best sites; normally lives 150-300 years, over 760 in Lapland; first-year seedlings have single serrated leaves 2-3 cm; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); growth and first cones from European yield tables

fruiting.source: Wikipedia (pollen released mid to late spring; first-year conelets globose, 4-8 mm; mature cones 3-7.5 cm, green then grey-green to yellow-brown; seeds released 22-24 months after pollination); crop and decay estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal: about six needle-like cotyledons; in full light first-year seedlings reach only 18-23 cm with soft single needles, and 46-64 cm by year three. Young trees are narrow, open, feathery cones of tufted blue-green needles that turn bright gold and drop in autumn; under a canopy they die, so they must stay in the open.
growth.source: USDA Silvics of North America vol. 1 (Larix laricina: germination late May-mid June, epigeal; seedlings 18-23 cm yr 1, 46-64 cm yr 3; mature 15-23 m; viable seed at 12-15 yr, large crops from ~40; good crops every 3-6 yr; usually 150-180 yr, max 335; very intolerant of shade).

fruiting.source: USDA Silvics (flowers late Apr-early May; cones ripen Aug-Sep, brown, oblong-ovoid, 13-19 mm; seed shed Sep through spring; vigorous open-grown trees up to 20,000 cones a year). Young-cone colour, set and persistence estimated.

canopy.name: Lodgepole pine

growth.juvenile_note: Epigeal seedling with 3-6 cotyledons and a tuft of single primary needles, then short, twisted, paired needles. Young trees are dense, narrow cones with regular whorls. Open-grown shore pines become bushy, crooked and flat-topped; inland trees become slim, straight poles. Serotinous cones stay closed on the branches for decades.
growth.source: USDA Silvics (Lotan & Critchfield): viable seed commonly at 5-10 years; ~3.6 m at 20 years on medium sites; germination peaks in the 2 weeks after snowmelt; very intolerant of shade; shore pine small and short-lived; ages commonly 150-200+, old high-elevation trees to 400+

canopy.source: western North American mountains; 20–35 m. Dense even-aged stands after fire; cones open in heat. Kew POWO for the name; standard floras for range.

leaf.note: narrow leathery evergreen leaves with strongly revolute margins, blue-green above, white beneath

growth.juvenile_note: Seedling: radicle first, two tiny cotyledons 11 days later, first true leaves at 18-28 days; at 6 weeks it is a slender upright shoot 1-2 cm tall on wet moss. It becomes sparse, upright woody stems with narrow, leathery, blue-green leaves with rolled-under edges and chalky-white undersides, creeping by rhizomes through sphagnum.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Andromeda polifolia: mean germination 13 d, light-dependent (66.5% at 25 C in light, 24-27% in shade or dark); cotyledons 11 d and first leaves 18-28 d after the radicle, a 1-2 cm shoot at 6 wk; plants 5-80 cm; shade intolerant. Growth rate, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Andromeda polifolia: 1-4 nodding urn-shaped flowers in terminal clusters, May-Aug by region; pollinated by bumblebees, honeybees, syrphid flies and butterflies; capsules 3-6 mm, 1-44 seeds, mature late Jul-Aug and often persist into winter. Fruit set and crop estimated; foliage contains grayanotoxins.

growth.juvenile_note: Extremely slow start: seedlings on moss are only 2 mm tall after a month and 4 mm after four. Tiny narrow leaves with rolled-under edges become the adult's leathery, strap-like leaves, dark green above and thickly rusty-woolly beneath. It builds a few thin, hairy stems, then spreads by rhizomes and layering into a low, open, aromatic evergreen patch.
growth.source: USDA FEIS Ledum groenlandicum (most seeds germinate in 25-30 days; seedlings 2 mm at 1 month, 4 mm at 4 months; flowers late May-Jul; capsules 4-6 mm ripen in fall; often >50 seeds per flower); Wikipedia (usually 50 cm, rarely 2 m; slow-growing; up to 35 flowers per cluster); ages estimated

fruiting.source: USDA FEIS Ledum groenlandicum (flowers late May-Jul; 352 flowers per 100 cm2 in good stands; capsules 4-6 mm ripen in fall; Apis, Bombus and Andrena bees visit); Wikipedia (small white flowers, petals ~1 cm, up to 35 per cluster; mainly bees, also butterflies and beetles; toxic in quantity); set, crop and capsule persistence estimated

shrub.name: Sheep laurel

growth.juvenile_note: Dust-fine seed germinates on moist bare peat or moss: a minute seedling with a pair of tiny leaves, then narrow leathery evergreen leaves in threes. For a few years a single wiry sprig; then it branches and spreads by rhizomes into a low, dense, evergreen colony, with rings of deep pink saucer flowers below the new shoots in early summer.
growth.source: FEIS Kalmia angustifolia (low shrub to ~1 m, strongly rhizomatous, bogs, barrens and burned heath; seed tiny and light-requiring); Flora of North America vol. 8; growth and ages estimated

It adds tillers every year, building a dense round tussock of stiff stems that turns orange-brown in autumn and winter.

ground.name: Sphagnum moss

growth.juvenile_note: A spore germinates into a tiny flat green plate that buds leafy shoots. The young colony is a soft cushion of fat, blunt, wine-red to purplish capitula (greener in shade) with swollen, spoon-shaped leaves, growing 1-3 cm taller a year in wet lawns and spreading into a spongy carpet.
growth.source: Springer Wetl. Ecol. Manag. 2019 (Chiloe, Chile: ~5.6 mm growth in 3 months, ~2 cm/yr); Diaz et al. 2012 Rev. Chil. Hist. Nat. (growth higher in lawns than hummocks); Bengtsson et al. 2016 (magellanicum-group 1-7 mm/yr in Sweden); shading aids regeneration (Can. J. Bot. 2025)

repro.note: spores by wind and water; no flowers; needs a wet film to reproduce, so spread reads moisture not pollinators

ground.source: Bogs worldwide; holds twenty times its weight in water and makes the peat; red in the open, green in shade. Kew POWO.

These become loose, glossy yellow-green, once-pinnate feathery shoots on conspicuous red stems with blunt, crowded leaves, adding roughly 1-2 cm a year and weaving into a springy carpet 3-10 cm deep. Most new patches start from broken shoot fragments.

repro.note: The mycelium is the organism and lives in the substrate for years; the fruiting body lasts days to weeks. 'rhizome' here = the mycelium spreading through soil, moss or wood; 'wind' = spores.

ground.source: Suillus cavipes, hollow bolete, Europe, Asia and North America, mycorrhizal only with larch including tamarack in bogs; cap 3-10 cm rusty-scaly, stem hollow — Index Fungorum; MushroomExpert.com

cap.form: convex to flat cap with a small umbo, dry, covered in rusty-brown fibrous scales
cap.notes: tawny to rusty brown, the margin hung with white veil fragments

underside.type: large angular yellow pores running down the stem

appearance.habit: scattered under larch (tamarack) on wet ground
appearance.seasonal: fruits in late summer and autumn
appearance.refs: Index Fungorum; Phillips, Mushrooms; MushroomExpert.com (Suillus cavipes)

associations.name: Sphagnum-cottongrass raised bog
associations.where: open bog center and hummock-hollow plain, rain-fed acid peat

associations.name: Heather-deergrass blanket bog
associations.where: gently sloping uplands with high rainfall, shallow peat over rock
associations.source: Scirpus cespitosus-Eriophorum blanket mire (Rodwell 1991 M17; Lindsay 1995)

associations.name: Black spruce-leatherleaf muskeg
associations.where: forested bog margin and slow-drained flats, deep peat, cold

associations.name: Bog pine hummock wood
associations.where: drier raised hummocks and bog rim on deep peat
associations.source: Pino mugo-Sphagnetum and Vaccinio uliginosi-Pinetum bog woodland (Ellenberg 1988; EU habitat 91D0)
